newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli lawmakers meet in PLO Jerusalem office.
newsitem.headline: Israeli lawmakers meet in PLO Jerusalem office.

text.p: A handful of lawmakers on an Israeli parliamentary committee visited Orient House, the PLO's Jerusalem headquarters, on Sunday in defiance of government policy.
Knesset Interior Committee chairman Salah Tarif of the opposition Labour party organised the visit, hosted by Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in the holy city.

"We came to visit Orient House to hear the problems of the residents of East Jerusalem," Tarif, a Druze Arab, said. He told reporters the visit, the first by Israeli legislators, was "very official" and that a majority of committee members had voted in favour of it.

Orient House, in Arab East Jerusalem, is a symbol of the PLO's nationalist aspirations and its desire to make the eastern part of the city, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, capital of a future Palestinian state.

Israel, which regards both halves of the city as its eternal capital, has warned the PLO not to conduct any activity associated with Palestinian self-rule at Orient House, saying Israeli-PLO peace deals restrict such activities to autonomous parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
The Palestinian Authority recently gave in to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's demand that it shut two Jerusalem offices as a precondition to progress in Israeli-PLO peace talks.
Tarif said Netanyahu's satisfaction with the closure of the offices removed any obstacles to an official parliamentary visit to Orient House.
But right-wing demonstrators countered that the offices had been moved but not been shut and that Orient House was an affront to Israeli sovereignty.
"Those bunch of terrorists fooled my prime minister," said Benny Elon of the far-right Moledet party.

Netanyahu, who last week rejected criticism from hardliners in his own Likud party who maintained the offices remained open, said on Sunday he had conflicting information and was checking into the matter.

"It is worthwhile that the other side understand that we will stand firm that these institutions be closed -- truly be closed," Netanyahu told Israel's Channel Two television. "It is a fundamental principle for the continuation of the (peace) process."
Tarif was accompanied by other Labour lawmakers on the 15-member committee, but right-wing and religious members boycotted the visit.

Lawmaker Zeev Boyem of the ruling Likud party, protesting outside Orient House, said the problems of Arab residents of East Jerusalem should be addressed to the Jerusalem municipality and not PLO headquarters.
"An address like this is an address that divides Jerusalem and this, it seems, is the stance of the Labour party," Boyem told reporters.
Tarif said that while it was government policy to oppose visits to Orient House by foreign diplomats, it had no authority to prevent elected Israelis from going to PLO headquarters.
The visit coincided with Israeli diplomatic efforts to persuade the fact-finding "troika" of the European Union foreign ministers not to hold talks with Palestinians at Orient House.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Saturday it was vital the troika visit Israel in the near future and also hold talks with the PLO, but he did not specify whether the talks would take place at Orient House.
